etymologies.etymologyHTML: From earlier craunch, cranch, of imitative origin.

definitions.definition: To crush something, especially food, with a noisy crackling sound.

quote.citation: 1816, Lord Byron, The Siege of Corinth:
quote.text: And their white tusks crunch'd o'er the whiter skull,

definitions.definition: To be crushed with a noisy crackling sound.
(slang) To calculate or otherwise process (e.g. to crunch numbers: to perform mathematical calculations). Presumably from the sound made by mechanical calculators.
To grind or press with violence and noise.

quote.citation: 1854, E.K. Kane, “The United States Grinnell Expedition in Search of Sir John Franklin: a personal Narrative”, in The Living Age‎[1], page 517:
quote.text: The sound of our vessel crunching her way through the new ice is not easy to be described.

quote.citation: 1921, Ben Travers, chapter 5, in A Cuckoo in the Nest, Garden City, N.Y.: Doubleday, Page & Company, published 1925, →OCLC:
quote.text: The departure was not unduly prolonged. […] Within the door Mrs. Spoker hastily imparted to Mrs. Love a few final sentiments on the subject of Divine Intention in the disposition of buckets; farewells and last commiserations; a deep, guttural instigation to the horse; and the wheels of the waggonette crunched heavily away into obscurity.

definitions.definition: To emit a grinding or crunching noise.

quote.text: There were sounds in the air above his head – sounds of the crunching and rattling of the loose, smooth stones as his neighbors moved about […]

definitions.definition: (automotive, transitive) To cause the gears to emit a crunching sound by releasing the clutch before the gears are properly synchronised.
(computing, transitive) To compress (data) using a particular algorithm, so that it can be restored by decrunching.

quote.citation: 1993, Michael Barsoom, “[comp.sys.amiga.announce] PackIt Announcement”, in comp.archives (Usenet):
quote.text: PackIt will not crunch executables, unless told to do so.

definitions.definition: (software engineering, slang, transitive) To make employees work overtime in order to meet a deadline in the development of a project.
A noisy crackling sound; the sound usually associated with crunching.

quote.citation: 1976 August 21, A. Nolder Gay, “Another View”, in Gay Community News, volume 4, number 8, page 4:
quote.text: It always pains me (slightly) when a flaming young radical like Neil Miller turns out when the crunch comes to be such an ardent defender of the status quo.

quote.citation: 1985, John C. L. Gibson, Job, page 237:
quote.text: The friends, on the contrary, argue that Job does not "know", that only God knows; yet, when it comes to the crunch, they themselves seem to know as much as God knows: for example, that Job is a guilty sinner.

definitions.definition: A problem that leads to a crisis.

quote.citation: 1994, Martin H. Wolfson, Financial Crises: Understanding the Postwar U.S. Experience‎[2], page 22:
quote.text: The crunch is characterized by extremely depressed liquidity and deteriorated balance sheet positions for households, corporations, and financial institutions […]

definitions.definition: (exercise) A form of abdominal exercise, based on a sit-up but in which the lower back remains in contact with the floor.

quote.citation: 2017 November 16, Jo Ellison, “Help: the gym has turned us into slobs”, in Financial Times‎[3]:
quote.text: But even I draw the line at “doing crunches” in designer clothes. Fashion sneakers are for swanking around the shops, not for running in. And so, like everyone else, I wear grotty old tracksuits earmarked for Oxfam, and tragic free festival T-shirts that give away my age.

definitions.definition: (software engineering, slang) The overtime work required to catch up and finish a project, usually in the final weeks of development before release.
A dessert consisting of a crunchy topping with fruit underneath.
(cooking, generally in the plural) A small piece created by crushing; a piece of material with a friable or crunchy texture.

quote.citation: 2014 December 18, “Fluffernutter and Nutella Yule Log”, in The Lovely Crazy‎[4]:
quote.text: Smear the peanut butter, fluff, and a bit of the nutella all over, even to the very edge of the wrap. Sprinkle the crunches on top and then start rolling from one of the non-trimmed edges

quote.citation: 2021 April 22, “Covid: India sets global record for new cases amid oxygen shortage”, in BBC News‎[5]:
quote.text: But a supply crunch, which is already affecting the drive, could slow it down further.
